output.brief:
The jump in chilled write-offs is mostly a receiving problem at your own DC, not a Haverlow problem. Haverlow's trailer data shows product at 2.4–3.5°C when doors open, with no alarms. The chambers held temperature. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four in week 31, night pallets wait a median of about 3h 52m (previously 44 min) on an unrefrigerated dock at 15–17°C. Probes are keyed at receipt confirmation, hours after unloading, so the 6.5–8°C readings reflect warming on the dock, not the trailer. Night write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier, including Pellridge and own-label, while day shift stayed flat. So a chargeback or volume move would punish the wrong party. Do not drop the probe either.
Next: restore night receiving staffing (or otherwise fix the dock-to-chamber time), set a maximum dock-to-chamber time monitored weekly, and withdraw the chargeback. Also check the probe timing. Customer credits are less clear: Corriebank's self-certification coincides with their rise, but some may be real spoilage from warmed product. Request claim-level data and reconcile a sample before changing credit terms. I'm fairly confident (about 85%) in the main finding.
